item.title: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
item.description:
The Italians were employed as technicians for the Italian branch of German arms manufacturer Rheinmetall. One Kuwaiti and one Pakistani national were also injured in the attack. Iran has denied involvement.

item.title: Gerard Depardieu to stand trial in France for rape and sexual assault
item.description:
Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.

Covered by 1 nonprofit, 2 public.
Sources: BBC News, Deutsche Welle, PBS NewsHour

item.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
item.description:
The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.

item.title: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes capsizes near Ibiza, killing one
item.description:
Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker capsized off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.

item.description:

item.title: Spain's De Cos chosen as next ECB president
item.description:
Former Bank of Spain governor chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde after winning support of EU’s biggest countries Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos has been chosen as the next president of the European Central Bank, to succeed Christine Lagarde, after winning support from the EU’s biggest countries. The economist and monetary policymaker will become the first Spaniard to lead the ECB, defeating his rival candidate Klaas Knot, the former head of the Dutch central bank. Continue reading...

Sources: France 24, The Guardian
